topic: Advancements in Open-Weights Large Language Models (2026)
transcript:
The Qwen team just dropped the open weights for Qwen 3.8, and this model achieves Opus level performance.

But you can actually run this on your laptop, not only that, Z.AI just dropped GLM 5.3.

A model that is competing with many of the frontier labs just through post training, and lastly, Codex is getting huge upgrades next week.

It's going to make the whole thing faster to use, so let's get into it.

So the Alibaba team just dropped the Qwen open weights yesterday.

And I think we got to give them some props because what they were able to accomplish with Qwen 3.8 is something that a lot of us are going to appreciate.

Because they basically created an Opus level model that we can technically run on our MacBooks.

Yes, you might need a little bit more of a decked out MacBook, but it is possible.

And if you have your own PC setup, this is a model that you can run on your own PC.

And not only that, it can also perform pretty competitively compared to all the models out there.

You're not going to get Fable 5 level performance or Mythos 5 level performance.

But if you're able to run a model locally that is getting performance similar to Opus 4.8, a lot of us will be pretty happy with that.

And if we take a look at the benchmarks and if we just take a look at what people have been creating with this model.

It it becomes clear that the open source labs have been accelerating development in 2026.

And the Qwen team particularly has accelerated their development in 2026 and have been able to achieve some remarkable results compared to last year.
